# <span id="aanchor18"></span> About Sources

Sources represent flowing product composition at strategic points in a pipeline. Product samples may be drawn into a sample cylinder for local or lab analysis, or continuously drawn and analyzed by an online chromatograph. In FLOWCAL, these types of sources are called "sample analysis" and "chromatograph" sources.

In FLOWCAL Gas, an online chromatograph may be connected to the EFM, which will perform weighted averaging of the analyses. This is called "RTU average".

#### Source Types

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Sample Analysis">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Sample Analysis</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Sample Analysis">

Sample analyses, or samples, are drawn locally either on a periodic "spot" basis or on a continuous "composite" basis. Sample frequencies typically range from monthly to annual.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 340;height: 630;" /> 

<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 301;height: 361;" />

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Chromatograph">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Chromatograph</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Chromatograph">

Online chromatographs are connected to the pipeline and continuously flow a small amount of product through a transfer line. The transfer line may either vent to atmosphere or be returned to a low pressure section of the pipeline. The chromatograph draws a sample from transfer line and analyzes it, which usually takes 2 to 6 minutes. The chromatograph controller will usually create hourly averages of components and properties from the individual analyses.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 509;height: 263;" />

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="RTU Average">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />RTU Average (Gas Quality Only)</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="RTU Average">

"RTU average" is a FLOWCAL-specific term that describes an online chromatograph (or other device) connected to the flow computer. RTU averages differ from chromatographs in two key ways. First, the flow computer will create weighted averages (based on flow rate or flow time), whereas the chromatograph can only create simple averages. Second, depending on the equipment in use, the analysis of an RTU average may be incomplete. Properties such as relative density and heating value, and components such as CO2 and N2, may be the only available variables.

</div>
